    Text version: case summary and full timeline

    Content warning: this page covers the deaths of three young children, a suicide attempt, and severe postpartum mental illness. Descriptions are factual and non-graphic. Help: Postpartum Support International 1-800-944-4773 · National Maternal Mental Health Hotline 1-833-TLC-MAMA · 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline 988.

    Case summary

    On January 24, 2023, at the family home in Duxbury, Massachusetts, Cora (5), Dawson (3) and Callan (8 months) Clancy died. Their mother, Lindsay Clancy, a labor-and-delivery nurse, then went out a second-floor window and was left paralyzed. She was charged with murder and related offenses in Plymouth County. It was not disputed at trial that she caused the deaths. The question was her mental state. The defense argued she was legally insane because of postpartum psychosis and overmedication. The prosecution argued she was criminally responsible and planned the killings. The 2026 trial in Plymouth County Superior Court ended in a mistrial on Sept. 4, 2026 after the jury could not reach a unanimous verdict. At a status hearing on Sept. 29, 2026, no retrial decision was announced, and further motions were set for Nov. 2, 2026. Lindsay Clancy is legally presumed innocent.

    Neutrality note: this is a neutral case study built only from public reporting, official releases and public court documents. It takes no side. Statements are labeled established fact, testimony by a named person, defense claim or prosecution claim. Times are Eastern Time. Many times on Jan. 24, 2023 are approximate. The site contains no images of the children and no scene or autopsy material.

    Timeline (131 events)

    1. Postpartum anxiety after earlier births (background)

      Oct 2019 (approximate) · defense claim · — · Medical history · Lindsay's account / defense

      The defense's position, stated in opening, is that she had postpartum symptoms after her second child and that this was significant because it can signal bipolar disorder (Reddington said an antidepressant like Zoloft in someone with bipolar disorder "messes with your brain"). Dr. Jennifer Tufts later testified Clancy reported trying Zoloft while postpartum with her second child. Exact dates are not established in the sources; placed approximately after Dawson's birth.

      Timing: Approximate: sources give no specific date.

      Sources: Lindsay Clancy trial: Patrick Clancy testifies ex-wife had thoughts of harming kids (WCVB, 2026-07-27); Lindsay Clancy trial testimony moves to psychiatrists who treated her before murders (CBS Boston, 2026-08-07)

    2. Third child, Callan, is born

      May 26, 2022 · established fact · Family home, Duxbury · Medical history · Evidence

      Callan Clancy was born on May 26, 2022 (date as reported in the Wikipedia overview, citing trial coverage). Cora was born in December 2017 and Dawson in September 2019. Lindsay Clancy took maternity leave from her job as a labor and delivery nurse at Massachusetts General Hospital.

      Sources: Killing of the Clancy children (encyclopedia overview; consulted for cross-checking and for items marked 'via Wikipedia') (Wikipedia, accessed 2026-09-29); Lindsay Clancy trial live recap of opening statements, ex on stand (NBC10 Boston, 2026-07-27)

    3. Begins telehealth psychiatric care with Dr. Jennifer Tufts

      Sep 2022 (exact date not reported) · testimony by Dr. Jennifer Tufts · Telehealth · Medical history · Evidence

      Clancy began seeing psychiatrist Dr. Jennifer Tufts in September 2022. Tufts testified that anxiety was the main concern and that she recommended individual therapy and sertraline (Zoloft); Clancy was concerned about side effects and initially did not start it. The family's nanny began caring for Callan that month as Clancy prepared to return to work.

      Sources: Lindsay Clancy trial testimony moves to psychiatrists who treated her before murders (CBS Boston, 2026-08-07); Lindsay Clancy weeps at autopsy testimony; jurors hear from former father-in-law, family friend (WCVB, 2026-08-06)

    4. Portal message asking to extend maternity leave

      Sep 30, 2022 · established fact · Telehealth portal · Medical history · Evidence, Lindsay's account / defense

      A Sept. 30, 2022 patient-portal message read in court said she had asked her employer to extend leave for postpartum anxiety/depression: "I don't feel mentally well enough to return to taking care of patients with a baby at home that still won't take the bottle."

      Sources: Lindsay Clancy trial testimony moves to psychiatrists who treated her before murders (CBS Boston, 2026-08-07)

    5. Starts, then stops, Zoloft

      Oct 2022 (exact date not reported) · testimony by Dr. Jennifer Tufts / Patrick Clancy · — · Medical history · Evidence, Patrick's account

      Per Tufts, Clancy began Zoloft after an early-October appointment, was "feeling pretty poorly" after starting it, and discontinued it. Patrick Clancy testified she took a total of seven pills of the Zoloft prescription before switching providers.

      Sources: Lindsay Clancy trial testimony moves to psychiatrists who treated her before murders (CBS Boston, 2026-08-07); Lindsay Clancy trial: Patrick Clancy testifies ex-wife had thoughts of harming kids (WCVB, 2026-07-27)

    6. Ativan prescribed for anxiety

      Oct 21, 2022 · testimony by Dr. Jennifer Tufts · Telehealth · Medical history · Evidence

      Tufts prescribed the lowest dose of Ativan on Oct. 21, 2022. On Oct. 26 Clancy reported less anxiety but continued insomnia and was using Benadryl to sleep; Buspar was suggested, but on Nov. 2 she said she had been "too afraid to start a new medication." Tufts discussed tapering Ativan because of dependency risk.

      Sources: Lindsay Clancy trial testimony moves to psychiatrists who treated her before murders (CBS Boston, 2026-08-07)

    7. Phone note: struggling to parent a third child

      Oct 25, 2022 · established fact · Phone note · Medical history · Evidence, Lindsay's account / defense

      A long note Clancy wrote on her phone on Oct. 25, 2022 was read to jurors by State Police Sgt. Timothy Chiappini: "I'm sad and depressed because I am not able to parent my third child like my first." The note also said she wanted to feel love and connection with all her kids.

      Sources: Lindsay Clancy Googled 'hallucinations' before killings (The Boston Globe, 2026-08-13); Key moments from Lindsay Clancy trial: What to know as jury weighs case of mom who killed 3 kids (CBS News, 2026-08-27)

    8. ER visit after going without sleep

      Nov 15, 2022 · established fact · Emergency room · Medical history · Evidence

      She sought emergency care on Nov. 15, 2022 after reportedly going two days without sleep; trazodone was prescribed. By mid-November her parents were visiting for days at a time to help. (Detail via the Wikipedia overview, which cites trial coverage.)

      Sources: Killing of the Clancy children (encyclopedia overview; consulted for cross-checking and for items marked 'via Wikipedia') (Wikipedia, accessed 2026-09-29)

    9. Journal entry about exhaustion

      Nov 18, 2022 · established fact · Journal · Medical history · Evidence, Lindsay's account / defense

      In an entry dated Nov. 18, 2022, read in court: "It's like I'm so desperate to get a mental break from taking care of everyone that my mind is trying to make something physically wrong with me."

      Sources: Key moments from Lindsay Clancy trial: What to know as jury weighs case of mom who killed 3 kids (CBS News, 2026-08-27)

    10. Referred to a South Shore perinatal mental health clinic

      Nov 20, 2022 · testimony by Susan Clancy / Dr. Jennifer Tufts · South Shore perinatal clinic · Medical history · Evidence

      Susan Clancy (Patrick's mother, a nurse) testified she reached out to colleagues running a program for postpartum mothers and that Lindsay was "begging for help." Tufts testified that by Nov. 22 Clancy had enrolled at a South Shore perinatal clinic and was going to start Prozac.

      Timing: Approximate: around Nov. 20-22, 2022.

      Sources: Lindsay Clancy 'said that she heard a male voice ordering her ... to kill her children,' psychologist tells jurors (The Boston Globe, 2026-08-18); Lindsay Clancy trial testimony moves to psychiatrists who treated her before murders (CBS Boston, 2026-08-07); Key moments from Lindsay Clancy trial: What to know as jury weighs case of mom who killed 3 kids (CBS News, 2026-08-27)

    11. Remeron and Seroquel prescribed by the perinatal clinic

      Nov 30, 2022 · established fact · — · Medical history · Evidence

      Around the start of December, the South Shore clinic had prescribed the antidepressant Remeron and the antipsychotic Seroquel (Tufts testimony about a Dec. 1 appointment). The Boston Globe's review of court records counted more than 30 prescriptions (13 psychiatric medications) from September 2022 to January 2023.

      Timing: Approximate: late Nov./early Dec. 2022.

      Sources: Lindsay Clancy trial testimony moves to psychiatrists who treated her before murders (CBS Boston, 2026-08-07); Lindsay Clancy case: timeline of prescriptions (The Boston Globe, 2026-07-27)

    12. December 'big spiral': suicidal statements, thoughts about the children

      Dec 2022 (exact date not reported) · testimony by Patrick Clancy · Family home · Medical history · Patrick's account

      Patrick Clancy testified that her "big spiral" began in December 2022: she said she was suicidal and had thoughts about harming the children. "The way she was describing it was that something might happen to the kids." He said he was not concerned for the children's safety: "She wasn't showing any intention of harming the kids." Her parents came to stay.

      Sources: Lindsay Clancy trial: Patrick Clancy testifies ex-wife had thoughts of harming kids (WCVB, 2026-07-27)

    13. Two crisis-hotline calls around the holidays

      Dec 2022 (exact date not reported) · defense claim · Phone · Medical history · Lindsay's account / defense

      Defense witnesses testified that Clancy called a suicide/crisis hotline (ASPIRE) twice around the holidays in late 2022. The defense says she was "turned away"; the Wikipedia overview reports neither hotline intervened because she did not have a plan to harm herself.

      Sources: Lindsay Clancy 'said that she heard a male voice ordering her ... to kill her children,' psychologist tells jurors (The Boston Globe, 2026-08-18); Mistrial declared in Lindsay Clancy murder trial after defense's appeal unsuccessful (Boston 25 News, 2026-09-04); Killing of the Clancy children (encyclopedia overview; consulted for cross-checking and for items marked 'via Wikipedia') (Wikipedia, accessed 2026-09-29)

    14. Nurse practitioner adjusts medications; bipolar disorder considered

      Dec 2022 (exact date not reported) · testimony by Rebecca Jollotta · South Shore perinatal clinic · Medical history · Other: prosecution / third-party

      Psychiatric nurse practitioner Rebecca Jollotta testified that Patrick attended an appointment and spoke with her by phone: "I believe he was concerned about her symptoms and he thought they started when she started being medicated." AP reported that one outpatient provider considered bipolar disorder in 2022, and that Clancy disagreed with that opinion at McLean.

      Sources: Key moments from Lindsay Clancy trial: What to know as jury weighs case of mom who killed 3 kids (CBS News, 2026-08-27); Lindsay Clancy trial spotlights psychiatric hospital stay before she killed her 3 children (AP) (PBS News / Associated Press, 2026-08-07)

    15. Mother recalls disclosure of fear of hurting the children

      Dec 2022 (exact date not reported) · testimony by Paula Musgrove · Family home · Medical history · Lindsay's account / defense

      Paula Musgrove testified her daughter sent texts asking her to stay the night and expressing concern about medications, and recalled a conversation in which Lindsay expressed a fear of hurting the children; Musgrove said she was not concerned because she was present.

      Sources: Key moments from Lindsay Clancy trial: What to know as jury weighs case of mom who killed 3 kids (CBS News, 2026-08-27); Mistrial declared in Lindsay Clancy murder trial after defense's appeal unsuccessful (Boston 25 News, 2026-09-04)

    16. Reports intrusive thoughts on Remeron

      Dec 1, 2022 · testimony by Dr. Jennifer Tufts · Telehealth · Medical history · Evidence

      Tufts testified that on Dec. 1 Clancy reported intrusive thoughts on Remeron and wanted to stop it: "She said it was a feeling like I am going to die." She denied suicidal ideation but said she was close to it. Tufts advised a single point of contact for medications after Clancy said she kept "reaching out to different people."

      Sources: Lindsay Clancy trial testimony moves to psychiatrists who treated her before murders (CBS Boston, 2026-08-07)

    17. ER visit for suicidal thoughts; declines inpatient care

      Dec 15, 2022 · testimony by Dr. Jennifer Tufts / Patrick Clancy · Massachusetts General Hospital ER · Medical history · Evidence, Patrick's account

      Tufts testified that at a Dec. 16 appointment Clancy said she had gone to the Mass General emergency room with suicidal ideation but declined inpatient treatment. Patrick testified providers recommended a postpartum program in Rhode Island. Lamictal (a mood stabilizer) was added around this time.

      Timing: Date of ER visit approximate (reported at Dec. 16 appointment).

      Sources: Lindsay Clancy trial testimony moves to psychiatrists who treated her before murders (CBS Boston, 2026-08-07); Lindsay Clancy trial: Patrick Clancy testifies ex-wife had thoughts of harming kids (WCVB, 2026-07-27); Killing of the Clancy children (encyclopedia overview; consulted for cross-checking and for items marked 'via Wikipedia') (Wikipedia, accessed 2026-09-29)

    18. One day at a Women & Infants (RI) postpartum day program

      Dec 20, 2022 · defense claim · Women & Infants Hospital, Providence RI · Medical history · Lindsay's account / defense

      Clancy joined a postpartum day program at Women & Infants Hospital of Rhode Island a few days before Christmas and was discharged after one day. The defense says the program indicated she was overmedicated; her civil complaint says the hospital ruled out postpartum depression and bipolar disorder based on an inadequate history.

      Timing: Approximate: 'a few days before Christmas' 2022.

      Sources: 'Go to God, baby': Lindsay Clancy files malpractice lawsuit, says she heard a voice ordering her to kill her children (Boston.com, 2026-01-27); Mistrial declared in Lindsay Clancy murder trial after defense's appeal unsuccessful (Boston 25 News, 2026-09-04); Patrick Clancy opens up about grief, the memory of his children and moving forward (CBS News / 60 Minutes, 2026-09-20)

    19. Suicide-related searches (disputed characterization)

      Jan 2023 (exact date not reported) · defense claim · Phone / household computer · Investigation · Lindsay's account / defense

      Investigators testified about searches on suicide methods; a Wikipedia page on suicide methods was accessed on a household computer in Aug. 2022, though they could not say who searched. Reddington cited a defense phone extraction showing a search about "how to slit your throat to die" and asked prosecutors not to describe the searches as "ways to kill"; he characterized them as searches for suicide methods.

      Sources: Lindsay Clancy Googled 'hallucinations' before killings (The Boston Globe, 2026-08-13); Courtroom hears harrowing 911 call in Lindsay Clancy case, as ex-husband recalls the day of children's killings (WBUR, 2026-07-29)

    20. Voluntary admission to McLean Hospital

      Jan 1, 2023 · established fact · McLean Hospital, Belmont · Medical history · Evidence, Patrick's account

      After returning to the MGH emergency room on Dec. 31 with persistent suicidal thoughts, Clancy was admitted voluntarily to McLean Hospital (Belmont) early on New Year's Day 2023. McLean psychiatrist Dr. Alia Goodheart first saw her Jan. 3 and diagnosed "major depressive disorder, severe without psychotic features," tapering an antipsychotic used for sleep.

      Sources: Lindsay Clancy trial testimony moves to psychiatrists who treated her before murders (CBS Boston, 2026-08-07); Lindsay Clancy trial spotlights psychiatric hospital stay before she killed her 3 children (AP) (PBS News / Associated Press, 2026-08-07); Lindsay Clancy trial: Patrick Clancy testifies ex-wife had thoughts of harming kids (WCVB, 2026-07-27)

    21. Discharged from McLean after about five days

      Jan 5, 2023 · testimony by Dr. Alia Goodheart · McLean Hospital · Medical history · Evidence, Patrick's account

      Goodheart testified Clancy reported she could sleep and was eager to be home for Cora's belated birthday party; she was discharged Jan. 5 with a two-week supply of Ativan and trazodone. "She had never stated that she had any thoughts of harming anybody else." The defense emphasized the team did not speak with her prior outpatient clinicians; Goodheart said she had not treated postpartum psychosis.

      Sources: Lindsay Clancy trial spotlights psychiatric hospital stay before she killed her 3 children (AP) (PBS News / Associated Press, 2026-08-07); Lindsay Clancy trial testimony moves to psychiatrists who treated her before murders (CBS Boston, 2026-08-07)

    22. Outpatient psychiatrist notes she is 'deteriorating'

      Jan 6, 2023 · testimony by Dr. Jennifer Tufts · Telehealth · Medical history · Evidence

      At a virtual appointment the day after discharge, Tufts noted Clancy appeared "deteriorating": "She appeared a little bit worse." Further appointments followed Jan. 9, 16 and 23 with medication changes.

      Sources: Lindsay Clancy trial testimony moves to psychiatrists who treated her before murders (CBS Boston, 2026-08-07); Lindsay Clancy case: timeline of prescriptions (The Boston Globe, 2026-07-27)

    23. Cora's belated birthday party

      Jan 7, 2023 · testimony by Patrick Clancy · Family home · Medical history · Patrick's account

      Per 60 Minutes, Lindsay made it home in time to celebrate Cora's birthday on Jan. 7. Patrick testified she seemed "much better" after discharge (as reported by E! News citing CNN).

      Sources: Patrick Clancy opens up about grief, the memory of his children and moving forward (CBS News / 60 Minutes, 2026-09-20); Lindsay Clancy's Search History, Apple Watch Data Detailed in Murder Trial (E! News, 2026-08-17)

    24. Civil complaint: hallucinations returned within a week of discharge

      Jan 12, 2023 · defense claim · — · Medical history · Lindsay's account / defense

      Her January 2026 malpractice complaint alleges auditory hallucinations for weeks before the killings, returning within a week of McLean discharge, including a voice saying "You will never be the same. The only option is to die." Prosecutors dispute this: they emphasize she never told anyone she heard voices before Jan. 24 (see trial testimony).

      Timing: Approximate: 'within a week' of Jan. 5 discharge, per complaint.

      Sources: 'Go to God, baby': Lindsay Clancy files malpractice lawsuit, says she heard a voice ordering her to kill her children (Boston.com, 2026-01-27); 'I'm so glad my children are safe,' Lindsay Clancy told chaplain after killing them (The Boston Globe, 2026-08-20)

    25. Texts with her mother: 'waiting for the day I wake up feeling like me'

      Jan 14, 2023 · established fact · Text messages · Medical history · Evidence, Lindsay's account / defense

      Texts read in court: on Jan. 10 she told her mother she was at the gym with her kids; on Jan. 12 her mother asked "still feeling a little better?" (reply: "A little bit"); on Jan. 14 she wrote "...hanging in there and waiting for the day I wake up feeling like me."

      Sources: Lindsay Clancy Googled 'hallucinations' before killings (The Boston Globe, 2026-08-13)

    26. Searches: 'schizophrenia' (8:58 a.m.), 'hallucinations' (10:33 a.m.)

      Jan 19, 2023, 10:33 a.m. EST · established fact · Phone · Investigation · Evidence

      State Police Sgt. Timothy Chiappini testified the phone was used on Jan. 19 to look up schizophrenia at 8:58 a.m. and hallucinations at 10:33 a.m. The defense cites such searches as evidence of emerging psychosis.

      Sources: Lindsay Clancy Googled 'hallucinations' before killings (The Boston Globe, 2026-08-13)

    27. Search: 'Can you treat a sociopath?', then psychosis (~10 min later)

      Jan 20, 2023, ≈ 8:30 p.m. EST (approximate) · established fact · Phone · Investigation · Evidence

      Four days before the killings, at around 8:30 p.m., the phone searched "Can you treat a sociopath?" (prosecution direct); on cross, Chiappini confirmed a search about psychosis about 10 minutes later. A search about benzo withdrawal was also made Jan. 20. Her complaint says she researched whether she was a psychopath.

      Timing: 'Around 8:30 p.m.' per testimony.

      Sources: Lindsay Clancy Googled 'hallucinations' before killings (The Boston Globe, 2026-08-13); 'Go to God, baby': Lindsay Clancy files malpractice lawsuit, says she heard a voice ordering her to kill her children (Boston.com, 2026-01-27)

    28. Last psychiatric appointment, the day before

      Jan 23, 2023 · testimony by Dr. Jennifer Tufts · Telehealth · Medical history · Evidence

      Tufts testified that on Jan. 23 Clancy reported "no motivation, numb" and said she had to force herself out of bed; she denied suicidal or homicidal ideation. "There were no signs of psychosis or mania." Tufts did not recommend hospitalization.

      Sources: Lindsay Clancy trial testimony moves to psychiatrists who treated her before murders (CBS Boston, 2026-08-07); Key moments from Lindsay Clancy trial: What to know as jury weighs case of mom who killed 3 kids (CBS News, 2026-08-27)

    29. Morning pediatrician visit with Cora

      Jan 24, 2023, ≈ 9:00 a.m. EST (approximate) · established fact · Pediatrician's office (off-site) · Day of (Jan 24, 2023) · Evidence

      Clancy took 5-year-old Cora to a pediatric appointment (Patrick testified she had become preoccupied with Cora's stomachache, per the Wikipedia overview). At arraignment prosecutors said the receptionist, nurses and doctor noticed no issues. Exact time not given in sources.

      Timing: Time unknown; 'morning'.

      Sources: 'She Killed the Kids': Prosecutors Outline Chilling Timeline in Duxbury Tragedy (NBC10 Boston, 2023-02-07); Killing of the Clancy children (encyclopedia overview; consulted for cross-checking and for items marked 'via Wikipedia') (Wikipedia, accessed 2026-09-29)

    30. Patrick: 'having one of her best days'

      Jan 24, 2023, ≈ 12:00 p.m. EST (approximate) · testimony by Patrick Clancy · Basement office · Day of (Jan 24, 2023) · Patrick's account

      Patrick, working from his basement home office, testified they exchanged photos of the children that day, including Dawson, who had dressed himself for the first time, and that Lindsay seemed happy, "having one of her best days."

      Timing: Time approximate (during the day).

      Sources: Lindsay Clancy trial: Patrick Clancy testifies ex-wife had thoughts of harming kids (WCVB, 2026-07-27); Courtroom hears harrowing 911 call in Lindsay Clancy case, as ex-husband recalls the day of children's killings (WBUR, 2026-07-29)

    31. Snowman with the children in the backyard

      Jan 24, 2023, ≈ 2:00 p.m. EST (approximate) · established fact · Backyard · Day of (Jan 24, 2023) · Evidence, Patrick's account

      Prosecutors said she went outside with Cora and Dawson, built a snowman and texted photos to her mother and husband with no sign of distress. WBUR reports the snowman was built in the backyard while Patrick worked in the basement office.

      Timing: Time approximate (afternoon).

      Sources: 'She Killed the Kids': Prosecutors Outline Chilling Timeline in Duxbury Tragedy (NBC10 Boston, 2023-02-07); Courtroom hears harrowing 911 call in Lindsay Clancy case, as ex-husband recalls the day of children's killings (WBUR, 2026-07-29)

    32. Her account: a loud male voice in the late afternoon

      Jan 24, 2023, ≈ 3:45 p.m. EST (approximate) · defense claim · Main floor (location not established) · Day of (Jan 24, 2023) · Lindsay's account / defense

      Prosecution rebuttal psychiatrist Dr. Avram Mack testified Clancy told him she heard a loud male voice in the late afternoon, saying "to the effect of, 'you should kill the kids, this is your last chance so that you can kill yourself.'" Her complaint says hallucinations and suicidal thoughts continued "nonstop" in the hours before. Prosecution experts said a single-occasion voice was unusual and that her accounts varied.

      Timing: 'Late afternoon' per Mack; exact time unknown.

      Sources: Lindsay Clancy told children "go to God" during murders, prosecution psychiatrist says at trial (CBS Boston, 2026-08-21); 'Go to God, baby': Lindsay Clancy files malpractice lawsuit, says she heard a voice ordering her to kill her children (Boston.com, 2026-01-27); Expert witnesses challenge claim that Lindsay Clancy experienced psychosis (The Guardian, 2026-08-25)

    33. Search: 'kids Miralax'

      Jan 24, 2023, 4:02 p.m. EST · established fact · Phone (room not established) · Day of (Jan 24, 2023) · Evidence

      The phone searched "kids Miralax" at 4:02 p.m. (prosecution timeline at arraignment; digital-forensics testimony also cited "Kids miralax" and "CVS pharmacy" searches that day). Prosecutors cast this as the start of a plan; the defense disputes that inference.

      Sources: 'She Killed the Kids': Prosecutors Outline Chilling Timeline in Duxbury Tragedy (NBC10 Boston, 2023-02-07); Lindsay Clancy's Search History, Apple Watch Data Detailed in Murder Trial (E! News, 2026-08-17)

    34. Search: takeout from ThreeV; Apple Maps drive time

      Jan 24, 2023, 4:13 p.m. EST · established fact · Phone (room not established) · Day of (Jan 24, 2023) · Evidence

      At 4:13 p.m. she searched for takeout from ThreeV, a restaurant in Plymouth, then used Apple Maps to check the drive time. In closing, prosecutor Jennifer Sprague cited this as evidence of planning.

      Sources: 'She Killed the Kids': Prosecutors Outline Chilling Timeline in Duxbury Tragedy (NBC10 Boston, 2023-02-07); Key moments from Lindsay Clancy trial: What to know as jury weighs case of mom who killed 3 kids (CBS News, 2026-08-27)

    35. Phone call to the Kingston CVS

      Jan 24, 2023, 4:47 p.m. EST · established fact · Phone (room not established) · Day of (Jan 24, 2023) · Evidence

      She called the Kingston CVS asking about kids' Miralax; the manager said it was out of stock but similar products were available. Manager Angela Krause testified it was a "normal interaction." (Oxygen reports 4:48 p.m.)

      Timing: 4:47 p.m. per arraignment timeline; 4:48 per another report.

      Sources: 'She Killed the Kids': Prosecutors Outline Chilling Timeline in Duxbury Tragedy (NBC10 Boston, 2023-02-07); Lindsay Clancy trial: Defense, prosecutors question Patrick Clancy; 911 call played in court (WCVB, 2026-07-29); Lindsay Clancy Trial Timeline: Her, Patrick Clancy's Day Before Kids Killed (Oxygen, 2026-08)

    36. Text to Patrick: takeout from ThreeV?

      Jan 24, 2023, 4:53 p.m. EST · established fact · Text messages (Patrick in basement office) · Day of (Jan 24, 2023) · Evidence, Patrick's account

      Text read in court: "Any chance you want to do take out from ThreeV" … "I didn't cook anything. It's been a long day." Patrick replied yes; she wrote "Okie dokie, check the menu when you can." He asked if Callan was up from his nap: "It was just a short nap." Prosecutors said ThreeV was farther than their usual takeout.

      Sources: Lindsay Clancy's Search History, Apple Watch Data Detailed in Murder Trial (E! News, 2026-08-17); 'She Killed the Kids': Prosecutors Outline Chilling Timeline in Duxbury Tragedy (NBC10 Boston, 2023-02-07)

    37. Dinner choices exchanged by text

      Jan 24, 2023, 5:06 p.m. EST · established fact · Text messages · Day of (Jan 24, 2023) · Evidence, Patrick's account

      At about 5:06-5:07 p.m. she said she'd have a Mediterranean Power Bowl; a minute later he chose a scallop and pork belly risotto.

      Timing: 5:06 per arraignment timeline; 5:07 per texts read at trial.

      Sources: 'She Killed the Kids': Prosecutors Outline Chilling Timeline in Duxbury Tragedy (NBC10 Boston, 2023-02-07); Lindsay Clancy's Search History, Apple Watch Data Detailed in Murder Trial (E! News, 2026-08-17)

    38. Order phoned in to ThreeV

      Jan 24, 2023, 5:10 p.m. EST · established fact · Phone · Day of (Jan 24, 2023) · Evidence

      She called ThreeV and placed the order. Hostess Saria Shelgren testified she had no trouble understanding the caller and it was a normal interaction.

      Sources: 'She Killed the Kids': Prosecutors Outline Chilling Timeline in Duxbury Tragedy (NBC10 Boston, 2023-02-07); Lindsay Clancy trial: Defense, prosecutors question Patrick Clancy; 911 call played in court (WCVB, 2026-07-29)

    39. Phone last unlocked

      Jan 24, 2023, 5:13 p.m. EST · established fact · Phone · Day of (Jan 24, 2023) · Evidence

      Digital forensics expert Ian Whiffin testified her phone was last unlocked at 5:13 p.m.

      Sources: Lindsay Clancy's Search History, Apple Watch Data Detailed in Murder Trial (E! News, 2026-08-17)

    40. Patrick leaves on the errands

    119. Mistrial declared

      Sep 4, 2026, ≈ 2:20 p.m. EDT (approximate) · established fact · Plymouth Superior Court · Legal · Evidence

      A third note read: "It is with a heavy heart that we report we are unable to come to a unanimous decision, and we will not be able to." The judge allowed one hour for an emergency petition; a Supreme Judicial Court single justice denied it, and the mistrial became official when court reconvened around 2:20 p.m. The split was 11-1 in favor of acquittal by reason of lack of criminal responsibility (per the defense and jurors). Juror names were sealed until Sept. 18.

      Timing: 'Around 2:20 p.m.' court reconvened.

      Sources: Judge declares mistrial in Clancy case after jurors, with 'heavy heart,' fail to reach verdict (WBUR, 2026-09-04); Mistrial declared in Lindsay Clancy murder trial after defense's appeal unsuccessful (Boston 25 News, 2026-09-04); WATCH LIVE: Lindsay Clancy returns to court for hearing to help determine whether she will be retried (AP) (PBS News / Associated Press, 2026-09-29)

    About this case study & method

    Purpose & neutrality

    This is a neutral reference. It takes no position on Lindsay Clancy's criminal responsibility, which was the central question at trial and remains unresolved: the jury could not reach a verdict, a mistrial was declared on Sept. 4, 2026, and as of Sept. 29, 2026 the District Attorney had not decided whether to retry the case. She is legally presumed innocent.

    It was not disputed at trial that Lindsay Clancy caused the deaths of her children. The dispute was her mental state. The defense argued she was legally insane because of postpartum psychosis and overmedication. The prosecution argued she was criminally responsible and planned the killings.

    How statements are labeled

    • established fact documented (records, surveillance, phone data, court rulings) and not disputed by either side as to the fact itself; interpretations may still differ.
    • testimony by X sworn testimony or first-hand statements by a named person.
    • defense claim and prosecution claim arguments or characterizations made by one side.

    The three perspectives

    • Lindsay's account: her statements as reported (to doctors, in the civil complaint, as relayed by witnesses) and the defense's framing.
    • Patrick's account: Patrick Clancy's testimony and public statements.
    • Evidence only: documented facts (phone and watch data, surveillance, records, rulings).
    • The timeline adds a fourth lane for prosecution claims and third-party testimony, so neither side's framing is left out.

    Limits

    • The 3D house is an approximate layout based on testimony and reporting, not official floor plans. Room positions are illustrative.
    • Many times on Jan. 24, 2023 are not precisely known (e.g., when the wounds occurred, the fall, responder arrival). They are marked approximate, with notes.
    • Where sources conflict (e.g., stair-climb data times, CVS distance, attribution of an opening-statement quote), both versions are noted.
    • The site avoids publishing the home's street number (the home now has another owner) and does not name jurors or private individuals peripheral to the case.
    • Quotations are short excerpts from the cited reporting. Check the linked sources for full context.
